title: Characterisation methods
examples: Can you show me an example of indirect characterisation?
What is the difference between dialogue and actions in characterisation?
How do I know when to use direct versus indirect characterisation?

explain.say: Today we will learn about characterisation methods in writing.
Direct characterisation is when the narrator tells you about the character.

items: The narrator states the character is brave.
The text says she was very kind.
The author tells us he was wealthy.

explain.say: Indirect characterisation shows us the character through what they do or say.

items: He helped the small child up.
She laughed at the silly joke.
He spoke in a very quiet voice.

explain.say: Actions are one way to show a character's personality indirectly.
Dialogue is what the character says, which also shows us who they are.
In real life, think about a character in a film you watched recently.

faq.q: What is the main difference between direct and indirect characterisation?
faq.a: Direct characterisation happens when the narrator explicitly tells the reader about the character. Indirect characterisation requires the reader to figure out the character's traits from clues like their actions or words.
asks: How do I spot direct characterisation?
Does indirect characterisation mean I have to guess?

faq.q: Can actions alone show a character's personality?
faq.a: Yes, actions are a very strong way to show character indirectly. If a character always helps others, we can infer they are kind.
asks: Are actions always enough to show everything?
What if the actions are confusing?

faq.q: Is dialogue the same as what the character thinks?
faq.a: No, dialogue is only the words spoken aloud. What a character thinks is usually shown through their thoughts or internal monologue, which is different.
asks: Does what they say mean what they feel?
Can I tell what they think from their speech?

faq.q: Do I have to use all three methods?
faq.a: No, writers usually mix them all together for a richer portrait. Using a mix makes your writing more interesting for the reader.
asks: Which method is the best one to use?
Can I just use dialogue all the time?

faq.q: If a character is described as 'loyal', is that direct or indirect?
faq.a: That is direct characterisation because the narrator is stating the quality directly to you. The writer is telling you, not showing you.
asks: If I say 'He stayed until dawn', is that better?

facts: Direct characterisation occurs when the author explicitly states a trait.
Indirect characterisation relies on evidence from speech, thought, or action.
Dialogue reveals a character's voice, education, and mood.
Actions often reveal a character's true values more than words.

quiz.say: The book stated that Maya was a very thoughtful and caring person.
quiz.show: The book stated that Maya was a very thoughtful and caring person.
quiz.why: The word 'stated' shows that the narrator is telling you the quality directly.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the narrator is not showing you through action or speech.
wrong.1: This is wrong because no words are spoken in this sentence.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the sentence describes a trait, not an action.

quiz.say: Because he immediately helped the fallen person up, John seemed very kind.
quiz.show: Because he immediately helped the fallen person up, John seemed very kind.
quiz.why: The reader infers kindness from the action of helping, which is indirect.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the narrator is showing the trait through an action, not stating it.
wrong.1: This is wrong because there are no spoken words in this example.
wrong.2: This is too narrow; it is the result of the action that shows the character.

quiz.say: When speaking to the teacher, Liam used very formal language and avoided slang.
quiz.show: When speaking to the teacher, Liam used very formal language and avoided slang.
quiz.why: The sentence focuses on the words used when speaking, which is dialogue.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the focus is on the words spoken, not physical movements.
wrong.1: While technically indirect, 'Dialogue' is the most specific and accurate term for analyzing speech patterns.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the description is based on how he spoke, not what the narrator said about him.
